title: cert-manager CRDs still serve v1alpha2, which 1.6 stops serving

detection.reason: read from the CRDs' own served-version list

quote: Following their deprecation in version 1.4, the cert-manager API versions `v1alpha2, v1alpha3, and v1beta1` are no longer served.
remediation: Convert every cert-manager manifest to `cert-manager.io/v1` (`cmctl convert` does it) and re-apply the 1.6 CRDs so only v1 is served.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.group | test("cert-manager\\.io$")) as $c | $c.spec.versions[] | select(.served) | select(.name != "v1") | "\($c.metadata.name) still serves \(.name)"'  # each row is a CRD serving a version 1.6 stops serving; NO rows = clean

title: cert-manager CRDs still serve v1beta1, which 1.6 stops serving

detection.reason: read from the CRDs' own served-version list

quote: This means if your deployment manifests contain any of these API versions, you will not be able to deploy them after upgrading. Our new `cmctl` utility or old `kubectl cert-manager` plugin can convert old manifests to `v1` for you.
remediation: Convert every cert-manager manifest to `cert-manager.io/v1` and re-apply the 1.6 CRDs so only v1 is served.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.group | test("cert-manager\\.io$")) as $c | $c.spec.versions[] | select(.served) | select(.name != "v1") | "\($c.metadata.name) still serves \(.name)"'  # each row is a CRD serving a version 1.6 stops serving; NO rows = clean

title: v1.6.0 fails JKS keystore renewals with short passwords — install 1.6.1 or later

detection.reason: keystore passwords live in Secrets, which are never collected; and the patch version you will install is not a fact of the current cluster

quote: In cert-manager `v1.6.0` JKS Keystores had a minimum password length of 6 characters, as an unintended side effect of upgrading keystore-go from `v2` to `v4`. If you are using a shorter password, certificates would have failed to renew, and the only observable error was in the cert-manager logs. This was fixed in cert-manager `v1.6.1`.
remediation: Skip v1.6.0 and install the latest 1.6 patch.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("cert-manager")) | .spec.template.spec.containers[].image'  # a tag of v1.6.0 after the upgrade is the one release to avoid
